Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0100", "row_sha256": "983562eb30915c1ffae629978165f5b1fb7db55f318fb41c2b5f3b782ccfea5a", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you turn this into one self-contained ordinary internal update about the Cedar Table Food Cooperative inventory, not a report or a big analysis. this is for members and the shop team who need to know what was counted and what still needs checking. the count was monday, october 14, 2024, after sunday close, between 6:45 and 8:10 in the morning before the doors opened. Sam, Lila and Omar did the count together. we should say that because it explains the timing, but it wasn't a count of every object or every kind of stock the co-op owns. the team checked the Brookside shop floor and the adjoining warehouse only. member-owned consignment goods, office supplies, orders still in transit and the personal lockers weren't part of this count. keep that limit attached to the inventory information so it doesn't read like a whole-building audit.

some of my notes are out of order, sorry. in dry goods there were 84 brown-rice sacks, 25 pounds each, in the shop and warehouse. nineteen sacks had already been set aside for pantry boxes, and the stock sheet still lists them within the total count, so don't make it sound like those are available for regular sales. the posted reorder mark for rice is 90 sacks. the lentil count was 17 cases and the posted reorder mark is 18. those two are the only items the count sheet marks below their reorder marks. the canned-bean count is 46 cases; the posted mark for beans is 40. don't turn any of the reorder marks into an order or say something has been purchased. the mark sheet was last updated on september 30, which might be useful context, but it isn't a statement that the marks were reviewed during monday's count.

there is also an oats number, but we need to be careful about what it says. the bulk oats bin was estimated at 31.5 pounds, not weighed as an exact final quantity. the floor scale showed a small drift when it was checked, and the scale was last calibrated september 26. service is booked for october 18. don't include oats with the below-mark findings because the amount is an estimate and the count sheet doesn't compare that estimate against a reorder mark. The shop kept the estimate on the sheet as a working figure until the scale check; it isn't a corrected inventory figure. i know that sounds like a small detail, but it changes how certain the number is.

for the cold and fresh items, the team counted 38 crates of apples. eleven crates had soft fruit and were moved aside for kitchen use, while the other 27 crates stayed on the shop display. there are 22 gallons of milk and 8 flats of yogurt in the cooler. three of the milk gallons have an october 16 use-by date. at 7:20 a.m. the cooler temperature was 38 degrees Fahrenheit. in the freezer there were 14 crates of frozen vegetables, and 5 of those were marked for the meal program. keep the apple separation and the meal-program marks as their own details; neither one means those quantities disappeared from the physical count. don't say that any other produce or dairy was counted, since it isn't in the notes.

there are some useful supply details too: 640 paper bags were on hand, along with six boxes of printed labels. Lila said, "We have enough lentils for the pantry run, but the rice shelf is tighter than it looks." include that as an ordinary comment during the count, not as a formal finding or a promise. the rice set aside for pantry boxes is why it should not be described as regular-sales stock, but the quote itself is just what Lila said; don't rewrite it into a new conclusion. there was a separate note on the delivery clipboard that an invoice listed six bags of flour. the flour delivery arrived after the count had ended, so those bags were not included in monday's count. This doesn't tell us that there are no other flour bags in the co-op, it only says these six weren't counted as part of that delivery before the count closed.

numbered section would feel natural for the count figures, maybe label it 1, Counted stock, and group the dry goods, fresh and cold items, and packaging without making it seem like these were separate days. Then have a paragraph that mentions the records and what is pending. On friday, october 11, a request for 10 more rice sacks was entered with the supplier. As of the monday count, the supplier had not confirmed it. This is a request entered, not an approved order, and there isn't a delivery date to give. the flour arrived afterward, as above, so mention that separately rather than adding it to the counted totals or treating it as a new result of monday's work. Keep the order status as of the count, not as if we know anything that happened later.

the final paragraph needs distinct information, not a recap. please keep the limit and the exact scope of the final assessment clear: based on the physical stock figures on the count sheet, rice and lentils were below their posted reorder marks; beans were above theirs; oats can't be compared because it remains an estimate and there is no mark recorded for it. The assessment is about those listed lines and posted marks only, not a check of prices, sales, demand, other locations or all cooperative supplies. the pending rice request is still unconfirmed as of monday. don't turn the assessment into an instruction to buy anything or announce what the co-op decided. make this one connected update, readable and factual, with that last assessment left as the last point rather than an added summary or recommendation.", "output": "Write one self-contained, ordinary internal update about the Cedar Table Food Cooperative inventory for members and the shop team. Keep it readable, connected, and factual—not a report or extended analysis. The count took place on Monday, October 14, 2024, from 6:45 to 8:10 a.m., after Sunday close and before the doors opened. Sam, Lila, and Omar counted the Brookside shop floor and adjoining warehouse. State the scope clearly: the count did not include member-owned consignment goods, office supplies, orders in transit, or personal lockers, and it was not a whole-building audit.

Use a numbered section labeled “1. Counted stock” for the figures, grouping dry goods, fresh and cold items, and packaging while making clear these were all counted on the same occasion.

- **Dry goods:** The shop and warehouse held 84 brown-rice sacks, 25 pounds each. Nineteen were already set aside for pantry boxes and are included in the total count, but should not be described as available for regular sales. The posted rice reorder mark is 90 sacks. Lentils totaled 17 cases against a posted reorder mark of 18. Canned beans totaled 46 cases against a posted mark of 40. These are the only items the count sheet marks below their reorder marks. The mark sheet was last updated September 30; do not imply that the marks were reviewed during Monday’s count. Do not say anything has been ordered or purchased on the basis of these marks.
- **Oats:** The bulk bin was estimated at 31.5 pounds; this was not an exact final weighing. The floor scale showed a small drift when checked and was last calibrated September 26. Service is booked for October 18. The shop retained the estimate as a working figure pending the scale check; it is not a corrected inventory figure. Do not include oats among the below-mark findings: the quantity is an estimate, and the count sheet has no reorder mark for it.
- **Fresh and cold items:** There were 38 crates of apples. Eleven crates with soft fruit were moved aside for kitchen use; the other 27 remained on the shop display. The cooler held 22 gallons of milk and 8 flats of yogurt. Three milk gallons have an October 16 use-by date. At 7:20 a.m., the cooler temperature was 38 degrees Fahrenheit. The freezer held 14 crates of frozen vegetables, 5 marked for the meal program. Keep the apple separation and meal-program marks distinct; neither means those quantities were absent from the physical count. Do not imply that other produce or dairy was counted.
- **Packaging:** There were 640 paper bags and six boxes of printed labels on hand.

Include Lila’s comment as an ordinary remark during the count: “We have enough lentils for the pantry run, but the rice shelf is tighter than it looks.” Do not present it as a formal finding or promise, or turn it into a new conclusion. The rice set aside for pantry boxes is a separate reason not to describe those sacks as regular-sales stock.

In a paragraph about records and pending matters, state that a Friday, October 11 request for 10 more rice sacks was entered with the supplier. As of the Monday count, the supplier had not confirmed it; it was a request, not an approved order, and no delivery date is available. The delivery clipboard also had an invoice listing six bags of flour. That delivery arrived after the count ended, so those six bags were not included in Monday’s count. Mention this separately from the counted totals. This does not establish that the cooperative had no other flour; it only describes the six bags on that delivery.

End with a distinct final paragraph giving the assessment, not a recap. State its scope precisely: based on the physical stock figures on the count sheet, rice and lentils were below their posted reorder marks, and beans were above theirs. Oats cannot be compared because its quantity remains an estimate and no reorder mark is recorded for it. This assessment covers only those listed lines and posted marks; it is not a check of prices, sales, demand, other locations, or all cooperative supplies. The rice request remained unconfirmed as of Monday. Do not make a purchase recommendation, announce a cooperative decision, or add a summary after this final assessment."}]
